## Function

FOXE1 encodes a forkhead transcription factor with established roles in thyroid and craniofacial development. Its promoter methylation has also been investigated as a marker in several cancers and in colitis-associated neoplasia.

::: {.gene-mechanism}
::: {.gene-state}
**FOXE1 expressed in its developmental context**

Coordinates lineage-specific transcriptional programs.
:::
::: {.gene-flow-arrow}
→
:::
::: {.gene-state .gene-state-off}
**FOXE1 methylated in colon samples**

May be a robust epigenetic marker even if the downstream colon-specific mechanism is unclear.
:::
:::

This distinction matters: a locus can classify tissue state because its methylation is reproducible, without its protein being a driver in that tissue. The cited UC panel paper reported FOXE1 methylation in a subset of UC samples but did not establish functional silencing as a progression mechanism.

<details><summary><strong>Biomarker versus driver test</strong></summary>

Confirm colon-cell expression and regulons before proposing a driver role; assess replicated methylation and prospective outcome association for biomarker use.
</details>
